You're not fighting because someone asked you to. That's why in wars between empires, these people usually win. They are much more motivated. Wealth, military power, and a productive hurting system likely brought prestige and power to identities associated with Indo-Uropean dialects after 33 BC.

Praise posture at public feasts encouraged patrons to be generous, validating the language of songs as a vehicle for communicating with gods who regulated everything. So, even though there are wealthy and poor people, they are still treated with respect in this very egalitarian society. The belief that if I do you a favor, then you owe me one maintains the system; the gods oversee these contracts.

It's easy to bring more people into this system, making it innovative, cohesive, and open. Young men enter secret societies like mafia gangs, becoming members of the Morabon, a warrior brotherhood bound by oath to each other and ancestors during ritual raids. These young men are essentially the Vikings' direct descendants.

The Mongols conquered most of the world; their secret weapon was the horse archer. The Yamnaya came first, conquering Europe, India, and Iran. Later, the Scythians, not a race but a culture, dominated. Then the Medians gave rise to the Persian Empire.

China emerges as the Han Empire, trying to destroy the Huns by moving a huge army into the grasslands, forcing them westwards towards the Roman Empire. This migration cascades through other groups, with the strongest staying in the steps and weaker ones conquering empires. Constant innovation drives this process; the Han Empire faces the Turks, leading eventually to the Mongol Empire's conquest of most of the world.
